# DIVERTICULITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

## Uncomplicated diverticulitis requiring admission or immunocompromised

Duration of therapy: Treatment duration depends on clinical response, typically requiring 7-10 days of antimicrobial therapy.

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Diverticulitis and Typhlitis
- Sanford Guide article: Diverticulitis
- Solomkin et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2010, 50:133-64
- Up-to-Date article: Acute colonic diverticulitis: Medical management
Therapy:
## Uncomplicated diverticulitis not requiring admission and not immunocompromised

Antimicrobials not indicated

## Complicated diverticulitis (perforation, abscess, fistula, obstruction) OR meets sepsis criteria OR patient is immunocompromised

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

Preferred: Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
< OR >
Piperacillin-Tazobactam 3.375g IV q6h [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

## Complicated diverticulitis (perforation, abscess, fistula, obstruction) OR meets sepsis criteria OR patient is immunocompromised

Consult General Surgery
Duration of therapy: Treatment duration depends on clinical response and source control, typically requiring 10-14 days of antimicrobial therapy.
Preferred:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]
< OR >
Meropenem 1 gm IV q8h [R,O]
Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
